evals.prompt: We added a new typedecide backend called acme-local. It returns a probability per option but its SDK rounds each probability to four decimals. Add 12 new rule-grounded cases across the existing benchmark families, run a one-case smoke test first, then benchmark acme-local against Laya for five repeats. Produce raw artifacts plus Markdown and self-contained HTML reports. Do not overwrite the existing 100-case artifacts.
evals.expected_output: A plan and implementation that validates new fixtures, treats rounded distribution normalization separately from model failures, uses new immutable artifact paths, performs a smoke test before the full run, and generates reproducible Markdown and self-contained HTML reports from raw data.
expectations: Uses uv and validates fixtures and offline tests before model execution.
Preserves existing benchmark artifacts and creates new output paths.
Separates rounded-probability normalization from model failure accounting.
Plans or implements raw JSON, Markdown, and self-contained HTML reports derived from the artifact.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied completed typedecide benchmark artifact. Generate a report for engineers deciding which backend to use. The report must show overall and per-family results, identify confident wrong cases, distinguish hosted versus local latency, include Jev token cost separately, and prove that every case is present in a self-contained HTML report with no API keys or external assets.
evals.expected_output: A reproducible report-generation and validation workflow, with concise conclusions grounded in the raw artifact and explicit caveats about authored cases and non-equivalent latency environments.
expectations: Does not manually invent or copy aggregate metrics; derives them from the raw artifact.
Includes per-family and case-level analysis, including wrong predictions and probability evidence.
Separates Jev hosted token cost from local backend cost claims.
Validates that HTML contains all fixture IDs and no external resources or secret values.
Generates structured HTML with cards, real tables, comparison bars, and case-level error markers rather than escaped Markdown in a preformatted block.

evals.prompt: I only changed a README example and want to run uv run pytest. Do not create a benchmark, call a model, or generate a report.
evals.expected_output: The benchmark-report skill should not take over this ordinary documentation/test task; the response should stay focused on the requested test run.
expectations: Does not propose live backend benchmarking or report generation.
Recognizes that no benchmark workflow is needed for this request.
